 THIS MFA IS FILED U/SEC.173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT,
 1988, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 21.04.2014  PASSED IN MVC NO.425/2012 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL  JUDGE AND MEMBER MACT-VIII, BADAMI, PARTLY ALLOWING THE  CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT  OF COMPENSATION.
 -2-  MFA No. 102200 of 2014  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging impugned judgment and award dated 21.04.2014 passed by Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT, Badami, in MVC No.425/2012, this appeal is filed by the claimants seeking for enhancement of compensation.
2.

Sri. Chetan S.Patil, learned counsel appearing for Sri. Shivaraj S.Balloli, learned counsel for claimants-appellants at outset submitted that occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle and liability of insurer is not in dispute as insurer has settled award passed by tribunal.

Learned counsel further submitted that claimants are seeking enhancement of compensation on limited grounds,
namely, monthly income assessed by tribunal was inadequate and award towards conventional heads was not proper.
3. Smt. Preeti Shashank, learned counsel for respondent-insurer does not dispute submission insofar as accident and liability of insurer.
She would however seek to support award on quantum.

4. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and record.
5.
Admittedly, deceased was aged 65 years.
Though claimants stated that he was earning Rs.3,00,000/- p.a. from agricultural, there was no specific evidence to substantiate same.
Records of rights produced do not indicate income or exclusive land holding of deceased.
In absence of specific evidence, same has to be assessed on notional terms.
Notional income for year 2012 is Rs.6,500 / -.
Therefore, Tribunal was not justified in taking it at Rs.3,000/-.
It has to be considered at Rs.6,500/- per month.
Tribunal has deducted 1/3 r d towards personal expenses and applied multiplier of '7' which is just and proper.
Thus, loss of dependency would be (Rs.6,500/- - 1/3 X 12 X 7) Rs.3,64,000/-.

Apart from above, they would be entitled to award of Rs.40,000/- each towards spousal consortium and parental consortium and also Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and since more than three years have lapsed after decision in Pranay Sethi, there has to be addition of 10% to award under conventional heads.

Consequently, following:
 ORDER a. Appeal is allowed in part.
b. Claimants are entitled for reassessed  compensation of Rs.5,79,000/- as  against Rs.2,38,000/- awarded by tribunal with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
c. Insurer is directed to deposit balance enhanced compensation within six weeks.
d. Out of enhanced compensation claimant no.1 is held entitled for 60% and claimants nos.2 and 3 entitled for 20% each.
Entire award amount apportioned in favour of claimants no.2 and 3 is ordered to be released.
25% of award amount apportioned in favour of claimant no.1 is ordered to be released.
Remaining amount to kept in fixed deposit for a period of three years in any nationalized bank.
